topic.title: Work with Large Files in Git

body.p: Git repositories are designed to track changes to text-based files, such as source code, and are optimized for small files. Large binary files, such as image or video files, can slow down the Git repository and make version control harder. Git Large File Storage (LFS) stores and manages large files outside the repository.

To start using LFS, follow the instructions at . After you install LFS and define the tracked large files in your repository, the Git Client automatically detects and handles large files.If you use a proxy, set the HTTPS_PROXY environment variable for Git operations that use LFS.
